summary: strutil-helpers-core ships encrypted dropper disguised as string utility
details: Package advertises itself as a lightweight string utility exposing only trim/capitalize/truncate, but index.js unconditionally require()s platform-specific native addons (native_win.node 434KB, native_mac.node 52KB, native.napi.node 17KB) at module load. The native binaries contain the format strings '%s/.napi_cache', '%s.nc%lu.js' and 'node "%s"' alongside CreateProcessA / execlp / fork / setsid / chmod primitives, consistent with decrypting the sibling 1.3MB high-entropy '.napi_cache' blob (sha256 d64c17b6cb7540add1c6a3087574f66e998ec0d972cf12c9ab7572379d81f01d, no printable strings) to a file under ~/.napi_cache/ and spawning node to execute it. The addons gate execution to real victim machines by enumerating CI environment variables (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER, CF_BUILD_ID), calling IsDebuggerPresent / CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent, scanning the process list for 'wireshark' and 'httpdebug', and inspecting /proc/1/cgroup, /proc/1/cmdline, /proc/self/status (TracerPid) and /proc/self/maps for containerd/dockerinit/tracer indicators. The declared purpose does not require native code, and none of the native/data payload is related to string handling. Any process that imports this package on a non-sandboxed developer or build host will execute the decrypted payload under node with the installer's privileges.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
